name: Vermont

notes: Food for home consumption is exempt.
Full-service restaurants and quick-service restaurants: not under the sales tax; taxed instead by the 9% meals and rooms tax.
Alcoholic drinks served are taxed at 10% under the meals and rooms tax, instead of the sales tax; a town's 1% local option meals tax applies to them too.
Barber and beauty services, laundry and dry cleaning, and auto repair labor: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).

Clothing and footwear are exempt, but not clothing accessories: jewelry and watches are taxed at 6% and counted on their share of US sales of clothing, shoes and jewelry (13%, 2022 Economic Census), 0.78% of what is spent on clothing, shoes and jewelry; the category's rate also takes in laundry and dry cleaning, at their own rate. Other accessories and sports or protective equipment are taxed too but not counted, since no official figure gives their share, nor is the 1% local option tax on jewelry.
Motor fuel is exempt from the general sales tax (per-gallon excise instead).
Some towns add a 1% local option sales tax.
Tobacco is assumed taxed at the general rate (excise taxes left out); not verified state by state.
gaps: Vermont local option tax (1%) applies only in the towns that adopted it. Vermont towns are county subdivisions, and those that are not Census places are matched to tracts through them. Counties levy no sales tax.
28 towns or townships that are not Census places have their rates listed here, matched to tracts through Census county subdivisions; each adds a local rate to the county's.
